newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran cleric slams EU, Germany over Berlin ruling.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric slams EU, Germany over Berlin ruling.

text.p: A leading Iranian cleric blasted the European Union on Wednesday for supporting a German court ruling that Iran's leaders ordered political killings abroad.

Ayatollah Ahmad Jannati, a senior member of Iran's powerful Guardian Council, attacked the 15-member EU at an evening rally of Islamic hardliners in Tehran with a fervour usually reserved for Iran's arch-foes Israel and America.

"When the European Union tried to bully us, the Supreme Leader (Ayatollah Ali Khamenei) hit them in the jaw so hard it made them understand the power of Islam," Jannati told a crowd of between 3,000 and 5,000 in a central Tehran square.

EU states broke off ministerial contacts with Iran and withdrew their envoys after the German court ruled in April that Iran's leaders were behind the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant. Iran denied the accusations.
Khamenei said Iran would not allow the German ambassador to return immediately after the EU decided the envoys could go back to Tehran. Tehran also withdrew its own EU envoys.
"They (EU) realised that the Imam (late Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini) is not dead. He is alive in other clothes," Jannati said in a 40-minute address to the rally.
Khamenei has headed Iran since 1989 when he succeeded Khomeini, who returned from exile in France to lead Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution.
Resolutions read out after Jannati's speech proclaimed the Berlin trial as a fraud and condemned the German government because of its actions in the affair.
Germany, until recently Iran's largest trading partner, was a leading supporter of the EU's policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran as an alternative to U.S. trade sanctions against Tehran.

"Israel, the European Union and the instigators of the Mykonos puppet show should know that as long as Iran has got its (clerical) leadership, Hizbollah and Basij, Iran will not bow before anyone but God," proclaimed a message delivered by megaphones and loudspeakers ringed around the square.

Black-clad young hardliners of the Ansar-e Hizbollah group, office workers, clerics, army conscripts and Basij militia volunteers made up most of the crowd in Vali-e Asr Square, which is usually full of shoppers and cinema-goers in the evening.
Jannati is a key force on the Guardian Council, a body of clerics and lawyers which has the power to reject legislation passed by the country's parliament.
The Council last week approved four candidates-- three of them Shi'ite clerics -- for presidential elections on May 23 and rejected 234 others who had signed up to run.
The four were selected based on their loyalty to Iran's religious system of government and "absolute obedience" to Khamenei, who has supreme power over all state institutions.
"No one can show the green light to the West even indirectly...If an official or others shows a green light to the West he is not one of us," said Jannati.

Posters flung from buildings and carried around the crowd by bearded, cropped-haired militants on pickup trucks called for the death of America and Israel and for fighting a Western cultural "invasion" -- a reference to the spread of Western lifestyles, clothing and music among Iran's youth.
